title: Jamia Millia Islamia agrees to hold student elections after weeks-long protest

ai.summary: Students at Jamia Millia Islamia university ended an 18-day protest after administration agreed to hold student union elections with a May 15 deadline for implementing the constitution.

facts.quote: Students at Jamia Millia Islamia university in Delhi ended their 18-day protest on Thursday after the institute’ administration agreed to their demands, including setting a timeline for restoring the students’ union.

facts.claim: Administration set May 15 as deadline for approving student union constitution
facts.quote: In an order issued on Thursday evening, the administration set May 15 as the deadline for approving and implementing the university’s student union constitution.

facts.claim: Elections would be held within six weeks of next academic session start
facts.quote: Elections would be held within six weeks of the start of the next academic session, or by the end of August, the order added.

facts.claim: University hasn't held student union elections since 2006
facts.quote: The university has not held student union elections since 2006.

facts.claim: Students protested since October 12 with five on hunger strike
facts.quote: Students had been protesting on the campus since October 12, with five of them going on hunger strike, to demand the restoration of the union.

facts.claim: University rusticated one student and suspended two on October 16
facts.quote: On October 16, the university rusticated one of the students on hunger strike, suspended two and banned all three from entering the campus for a year.

facts.claim: University revoked disciplinary actions on Thursday
facts.quote: However, on Thursday it revoked all disciplinary action against protesting students.
The university also said that in-person classes for all courses would resume on Monday and end-semester examinations would also be held offline.

facts.claim: Students alleged pressure to sign agreement
facts.quote: They alleged that they had been pressured into signing the agreement.

facts.claim: Delhi Police detained more than 70 students since October 12
facts.quote: They also said that the Delhi Police had detained more than 70 students since October 12.

ai.background_note: Jamia Millia Islamia is a university in Delhi, not Panjab University. The movement listed is for Panjab University staff, but this article is about Jamia Millia Islamia students. This is a mismatch.
